title: Chamfers or Radius and Relief Grooves on Toothing and Involute Splined
topics: Chamfers on toothing and involute splines
Relief grooves on toothing and involute splines
rules: When fitting coupling slide-guide is not possible, a chamfer with grinding wheel on tooth's edge must be made (see picture D015DA)
Chamfer at 15° for inner involute splined must be made in all cases, except for splined toothing intended for assembly with rotating discs (e.g., flanged hub or brake's housing)
Radius R (indicated in picture) must be made where necessary for fitting axe or centring in next machining processes
Tolerance must be an angle value different to 30° to respect condition of fitting with engraved angle
dimensions: Depth dimension: 0.5 units shown in drawing D015C
Relief groove depth: 9 x 45° shown in drawing D015E
tolerances: Angle tolerance must differ from 30° to respect fitting with engraved angle condition
manufacturing_notes: For internal splines, chamfer is 15° in all cases except for splined toothing intended for assembly with rotating discs (flanged hub or brake housing)
Use radius R for fitting axle or centering in next machining processes
When slide-guide coupling fitting is not possible, perform chamfer with grinding wheel on tooth edge
Relief groove must accommodate subsequent machining operations for assembly
training_guidance: NX agent must create 15° chamfer on internal involute splines by default unless the spline is intended for rotating disc assembly
For external splines on shafts where slide-guide is not feasible, apply grinding wheel chamfer per D015DA
Apply radius relief R at spline ends when required for axle fitting or centering operations
Ensure chamfer angle is not exactly 30° to avoid interference with engraved angle mating features
Model relief grooves with 9 x 45° geometry per D015E when axial clearance is needed for subsequent operations
Use drawing reference D015C for standard internal spline chamfer geometry with 0.5 depth and 15° angle
summary: This standard defines chamfer and relief groove requirements for toothed and involute splined components. Internal splines require a 15° chamfer in most cases, except when interfacing with rotating discs, while external splines may need grinding wheel chamfers when slide-guide coupling is impractical. Relief radii and grooves are specified to facilitate assembly and subsequent machining operations, with angle tolerances deliberately avoiding 30° to prevent interference with engraved angle features.
